source_documents.title: An AIE and PET fluorescent probe for effective Zn(II) detection and imaging in living cells

reference_evidence_units.quote: the fluorescence intensity of probe L increased 50-fold from 0 % to 100 %
reference_evidence_units.subject: L

reference_evidence_units.quote: However, with the increasing fraction of water, the rotation of C = C double bond was limited to some extent, which leads to the enhancement of fluorescence intensity
reference_evidence_units.subject: L

reference_evidence_units.quote: In low water fractions, the smoothly photoinduced electron transfer between tetrastyrene and N donor suppressed its emission.
reference_evidence_units.subject: L
reference_evidence_units.statement: PET from the N donor quenches the TPE emission.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: No energetics, electrochemistry or control compound.

reference_evidence_units.quote: due to the interruption of the PET phenomenon on pure probe L
reference_evidence_units.subject: L-Zn2+
reference_evidence_units.statement: Zn2+ chelation interrupts PET and turns emission on.

reference_evidence_units.quote: An AIE and PET fluorescent probe for effective Zn
reference_evidence_units.subject: L
reference_evidence_units.statement: The paper presents AIE and PET as the probe's two principles.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Title claim; the Zn2+ switching of PET concerns the complex.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: AIE is explained by restricted C=C rotation of the TPE unit in aggregates; co-equal with PET in the title.

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: PET from the nitrogen donor is said to quench the free probe at low water fractions; the title names AIE and PET as the probe's principles. Weak: no energetics, electrochemistry or control compound; role kept as the paper's (guideline §3.4, weak-evidence primary).
